note.title: Perfect or imperfect?
note.overview: Choose between the perfect and imperfect from the meaning of the event.
learningGoals: Use both tenses in one sentence when needed.
Explain why a tense fits the context.
mustMemoriseRules: Perfect = completed event viewed as a whole.
Imperfect = repeated habit, description, state or ongoing background.
One sentence may legitimately contain both.
workedExamples: Il pleuvait quand nous sommes arrivés.
Tous les jours, nous prenions le métro. / Hier, nous avons pris le métro.
commonMistakes: Choosing tense only from the English verb.
Assuming every past sentence uses the perfect.
Using imperfect for a one-off completed event.

French accents are corrected and displayed, but a missing accent alone does not lose the mark in this app.
